sun.upright:
Most Aries Suns I know would sooner start three things than finish one. You're cardinal fire, ruled by Mars, and a lot of your sense of who you are comes from going first. Temperance is the card of Sagittarius, four signs round the wheel from you and made of the same fire. That's a trine, the easiest angle there is, so this card won't feel like a lecture. It's more like a friend who happens to be better at pacing than you are.

The catch with fire meeting fire is that it turns everything up, including the bits you'd do well to turn down. Temperance is about patience and getting the mix right, and an Aries Sun can hear 'be patient' and make a contest of it, determined to be the most patient person in the building by Friday. The Emperor is Aries's own Major, a man on a stone throne who got where he is by taking charge. The angel in this card isn't in charge of anything. It's standing in a pool, pouring water carefully from one cup into the other. That's the kind of pride on offer to you, the pride of doing one thing steadily for long enough that it comes right, and I suspect it's harder for you than a fight would be.

At work it's the project you opened with a lot of noise that's now in its long, dull middle, where nobody's watching. In the body it's training, or any pace you've set yourself that's running too hot, the sort that ends with a pulled calf. Pick the one thing you're rushing and give it an extra fortnight before you judge how it's going.
sun.reversed:
Temperance upside down for an Aries Sun usually looks like all or nothing. You're either flat out on something, sleeping five hours and telling anyone who'll listen, or you've dropped it completely because it didn't take off fast enough. There's no middle speed. The trine with Sagittarius doesn't help, since the two signs egg each other on, and Mars never much cared for brakes.

At work you'll see it in a run of good starts that nobody got to see finished. In the body it's a cycle of hard training, a strain, and then weeks of nothing. People close to you may have learnt not to get too excited about your new plans, which stings if you notice it. Take the last thing you dropped and do twenty minutes of it, at a pace that bores you, three times this week.

moon.upright:
You feel things fast and you want them dealt with fast. A mood arrives, and within the hour you've gone for a run, sent the text or had the argument, and by dinner it's over. That's an Aries Moon. Mars rules Aries, so feelings in you tend to come out as action. Temperance is a Sagittarius card, another fire sign, and fire recognises fire, so the card is on friendly terms with your inner weather. It's still asking for something you don't do naturally.

What it wants is a gap between the feeling and the move. Your instinct says a bad mood is a problem and problems get fixed straight away. Temperance says some feelings need a night, time to mix with everything else you feel, and what comes out the other side is usually milder and easier to act on. The trouble with a trine in the same element is that the card can feed the heat as well. You get keen on calming down, and then cross when the calm doesn't turn up on schedule, which I've seen more than once with Aries Moons.

At home it shows as wanting to clear the air the minute something's off, when the other person needs until morning. In your body it's sleep, because an Aries Moon often goes to bed still revved from the day. When something upsets you, write the message you want to send, leave it in drafts, and read it again after breakfast.
moon.reversed:
The reversed card tends to show up in an Aries Moon as anger standing in for something softer. Anger at least moves, so when you're hurt or frightened you get cross instead, at the traffic, at your partner for breathing loudly, and the real feeling underneath never gets looked at. Sagittarius, the card's sign, would sooner look at the bright side than the sore spot, and between the two of you the hurt can go unfelt for weeks.

It shows in sleep first, lying awake braced for a fight that finished days ago. With family a small thing sets you off out of all proportion, and afterwards you can't quite explain why. Next time you feel the flare, ask yourself what you'd be feeling if you weren't allowed to be angry, and say that one out loud, even if it's only to the dog.

rising.upright:
Aries rising tends to arrive a second before the rest of you does. Mars rules your chart, so strangers read you as quick, direct, maybe a bit of a challenge, the one who speaks first in the meeting and already has a view on the coffee. Temperance sitting on that doorway smooths the edges a little. It's a Sagittarius card, trine to Aries and made of the same fire, so the two styles get on. Both are warm and both lean forward, and people like that about you.

The difference is timing. Aries goes in at full volume. The card suggests starting at about two-thirds and letting the rest come as the room warms up, and you may have noticed your usual entrance landing a bit heavy lately, with people stepping back half a pace when you come in hot. Your reflex is to read that as a cue to push harder, which gets it backwards. Same-element pairings turn things up, so the pull to overdo a first impression is stronger than usual, and the card's gift, if you take it, is a kind of ease that strangers read as confidence.

In interviews you might oversell in the first five minutes. In a new team an early push for change can make you look as though you haven't listened yet. On a first date it's the difference between charming someone and wearing them out. Walk into the next new room, find the quietest person there, and ask them a question before you say anything about yourself.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on an Aries Ascendant, Temperance can look like someone who can't do anything at half speed. You come in hot, stay hot and fill every pause, and because the card's sign is fire as well, nothing in the pairing takes the heat down. People meet a lot of energy and struggle to find the person under it.

There's a quieter form of it that's just as common. You've been told you're too much, so you've clamped the whole front down and come across stiff and oddly careful, which isn't you either. Both turn up in first meetings that never become second ones, in a new job where colleagues keep their distance, and in dating. Mars rules your chart and likes to act first. Try arriving somewhere five minutes early and just sitting there, so you're settled before anyone meets you.

sun.upright:
Taurus Suns can wait out almost anyone, so the patient side of Temperance will feel familiar. The part that won't is the mixing. This is a card about blending, a bit of this poured into a bit of that until it tastes right, which means something is always being adjusted. Taurus is fixed earth, ruled by Venus, and you got the recipe right years ago and would quite like to be left alone with it.

The card belongs to Sagittarius, five signs from yours. That's a quincunx, an angle between two signs with nothing in common, and it works by constant small adjustment. Fire and earth are neutral elements too, so there's no natural warmth to smooth things over. What you'll feel is something restless and a bit foreign turning up in a life built for steadiness, asking you to try a new route, a new way of doing the job, a trip you'd normally turn down. It never becomes one big clean decision, which is the frustrating part for you. It's a hundred small tweaks, and Taurus would much prefer to decide once and be done. The Hierophant is your sign's own Major, the card of how things have always been done, and you'll feel its pull against this one.

At work it's the method you've used for years that could do with an update, and you probably already know which. With money it's a habit of holding on, savings sitting in the one account that pays almost nothing, say. Change one settled thing on purpose and give it a month before you decide it was a mistake.
sun.reversed:
When Temperance is reversed for a Taurus Sun, steadiness can turn into not moving at all. Every suggestion that you adjust something gets a polite nod and no change. You keep the old arrangement going because you've always had it, and letting it go would mean admitting some of the years you put into it weren't well spent. The quincunx with Sagittarius keeps nudging, and you keep not noticing the nudge.

Venus can push it the other way, into too much of a good thing, the second helping, the expensive habit, the comfort that's stopped being comfortable and become routine. Look for it in money tied up in something that stopped paying off a while back, and in a partner who's asked for a change more than once. Pick one thing you hang onto for no good reason any more and let it go, even if you don't enjoy doing it.

moon.upright:
There's a lot in Temperance a Taurus Moon would like. It's slow and calm, nothing in the picture is in a hurry, and your feelings do best when the ground stays still and meals turn up when they're meant to. Venus rules Taurus, so safety for you is physical, the good blanket, the familiar walk, the person in the usual chair. Where the card and your Moon part company is its sign. Sagittarius is five signs away, a quincunx, and it's fire against your earth, two elements that don't dislike each other and don't warm to each other either.

So the card comes in wanting something new folded into the mix, a new habit, a new feeling, a slightly different week, and your body reads new as unsafe before your head has had a say. You may find yourself tensing at small changes that wouldn't bother anyone else, a friend moving dinner to a different restaurant, a partner wanting a different routine on Sundays. That's how a Taurus Moon keeps itself steady, and there's nothing wrong with it. Temperance just wants one new thing let in slowly, slowly enough that your body has time to decide it's fine.

Food and sleep will show it before anything else does, the comfort snack you reach for without thinking, the night you can't settle because something shifted during the day. It can show with a person you see mostly out of habit. Add one small new thing to your week, on the same day each week, and keep it there until it stops feeling new.
moon.reversed:
Comfort that's stopped comforting is the usual sign of this card reversed in a Taurus Moon. Same dinner, same show, same evening, and a flat, heavy feeling under all of it, because the part of you that only feels safe when nothing moves has taken over. The feeling that wanted to shift has settled into the body instead, and it sits there.

Sometimes the body gets more than it needs. A bit too much eating or drinking or shopping, because Venus rules this Moon and the quickest reassurance is something nice. You'll find it at home, in a room that hasn't changed in years, and in how you react when someone suggests a weekend away. Go for a slow walk somewhere you've never walked before and pay attention to what your body does with it.

rising.upright:
People tend to relax around Taurus rising. You come across as calm and unhurried, easy to be with, someone who won't be rushed, and Venus as your chart ruler usually gives you a good eye for clothes and a pleasant voice. Temperance on that front door adds something Taurus doesn't have much of by nature, which is movement. It's a Sagittarius card, fire, and Sagittarius sits at a quincunx to your rising sign, so the two share next to nothing. There's no natural bridge between how you usually begin things and how this card would. You build one on purpose or it doesn't get built.

You may already feel it as a mild impatience with your own first move. The calm, wait-and-see opening that serves you so well can also make you the last person to say yes to anything, and the chance goes to someone quicker. Sagittarius arrives open and a bit reckless. Temperance takes that and mixes it with your steadiness, so the version on offer is someone calm who also says yes, and people find that combination very easy to trust.

In a new job you might be read as solid but slow to join in. In dating, waiting to be sure can look like not being interested at all. At a party it's staying on the edge of the group you actually wanted to talk to. When the next invitation comes, answer it the same day.
rising.reversed:
With Temperance reversed, Taurus rising's calm can harden into a front that never changes. Something underneath has shifted, a job going badly, a relationship cooling, and your face and manner carry on exactly as before. People read that as all being well. They stop offering help, and you end up the last to admit a plan isn't working.

Venus rules your chart and likes things pleasant, so there's also a habit of smoothing everything over at the door, agreeing to plans you don't want because it's easier than a small bit of friction. In a new workplace you can seem fixed before anyone knows you, and in friendships people may have quietly learnt to work around you. Next time someone asks how you are, give a true answer, even a short one.

sun.upright:
Temperance belongs to the sign directly across the wheel from you. Sagittarius is Gemini's opposite, the other end of the same axis, and signs facing each other like that work as a pair. Gemini, mutable air, ruled by Mercury, collects things, facts, people, projects, open tabs. Sagittarius, ruled by Jupiter, wants to know what any of it adds up to. For a Gemini Sun this card is the other half of a conversation you've been having with yourself for years.

The friendly part is that fire and air get on. Air feeds fire, so the pull toward the far end of your axis is lively and a bit exciting, nothing like a telling-off. What you'll feel is a push from breadth to depth, from ten projects half done toward the one that means something. The Lovers is Gemini's own Major, and it's a card about choosing. Temperance is a card about mixing, which is better news for you. It wants to know which of the ten belong together, and there may be fewer loose ends than you thought. The Gemini Suns I've seen are often happiest when their side interests turn out to feed one bigger thing, when the podcast and the day job and the language class start pointing the same way.

At work it's the pile of things you keep half alive so none of them has to be judged. In friendships it's the way you'll circle a real conclusion for months and talk about everything but. Which two of the things you're juggling could become one?
sun.reversed:
The Gemini knack for a clever reframe gets a lot of use when this card is reversed. Nothing's ever finished, it's on hold. Nothing failed, it's pivoting. Every time something asks you to settle, Sagittarius, across the axis, hands you a bigger and more interesting idea to chase, and the loop stays open. You're busy all the time and oddly short of anything to show for it.

It can run the opposite way, too, into a flat, bored spell where none of your interests seem to mean anything and you've lost the thread that joined them. At work that looks like the projects you describe at parties and never ship. With friends it's being great company and hard to pin down. Close one thing properly, with an email or a final payment or a goodbye, and don't open anything new for a week after.

moon.upright:
Gemini Moons are good at mixed feelings. You can be glad and jealous about the same news, homesick and relieved in the same afternoon, and you usually know it, because Mercury rules Gemini and you're forever putting words to what's going on inside. Look at the two cups in Temperance. The angel isn't choosing between them. The water goes back and forth until it's the same all through, and that's what the card is offering your Moon, a way for two feelings to become one you can live with, without having to argue yourself into either.

Sagittarius, the card's sign, is Gemini's opposite, and the opposition shows in how each handles a mood. You break it into pieces and discuss them. Sagittarius steps back and asks what it all means. Air and fire get on, so the conversation between the two comes easily. The catch is that your usual relief, talking, can keep a feeling at arm's length. You can describe your mood in funny, accurate detail to three friends and still not have felt it, and some part of you notices. What helps here is letting one feeling go unnarrated for a while.

Sleep is where it shows first, the head that won't go quiet enough for anything else to get through. It shows with a sibling or an old friend, where things have cooled and you've kept it light with jokes. Next time something stirs you up, don't message anyone about it for a day, and see what's left of the feeling by then.
moon.reversed:
Noise is the giveaway when Temperance is reversed for a Gemini Moon. A podcast on while you cook, a group chat going while you watch something, a change of subject the second a conversation gets close to anything real. The quiet is where feeling happens, so you've arranged for there to be none. Sagittarius, opposite your Moon, keeps offering something bright and interesting to think about next, which doesn't help.

Two in the morning is when it catches up with you, the mind running through the same five thoughts in a different order. It's there in being cheerful with friends when you aren't, and in messages sent faster than they were thought through. Mercury rules this Moon and likes to understand things, and some things only make sense once they've been felt. Leave the phone in another room for one evening and let yourself be a bit bored.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising makes a quick first impression, and usually a funny one. You're curious, easy to talk to and a bit hard to pin down, and with Mercury as your chart ruler the first thing people notice is often your mouth or your hands. Temperance on that front door comes from Sagittarius, the sign straight across from your Ascendant. The seventh house begins on the sign opposite the rising, so Sagittarius already sits on the cusp of your partnerships. It's the kind of person you're drawn to, and the kind of thing people want from you once they know you.

That makes this card feel oddly familiar at the door. It asks you to lead with a little more weight, one thing you actually believe in place of five things you find interesting. Air and fire are friendly, so this won't cost you your lightness, and people who'd usually enjoy you and forget you may start remembering what you said. There's some friction, as there always is with an opposition, because your instinct is to keep moving in a conversation and this card wants you to stand still on a point.

In interviews and pitches you might skip across ten strengths when one real example would do more. At a party it's the person who asks you a serious question and gets a joke back. Before the next meeting that matters, decide the one thing you'd like them to walk away with, and say it early.
rising.reversed:
Cleverness becomes cover when Temperance is reversed on a Gemini Ascendant. The talk stays fast and bright, the jokes land, and nobody gets close enough to see that the opening move stopped working a while ago. Sagittarius, opposite your rising, adds a taste for the big claim, so you may also be promising more in first meetings than you'd want to be held to.

People find you excellent company and somehow hard to reach, and they stop bringing you anything heavy. That can feel like being liked and lonely at once. Dating shows it, when the banter goes on for weeks and nothing deepens, and so does work, where a good pitch gets you in and the follow-up doesn't match it. In the next pause in a conversation, don't fill it. Count to five and let the other person go first.

sun.upright:
There's a detail in the Temperance picture a Cancer Sun might like. The angel stands with one foot in the water and one on dry land, which is more or less where you live, in the feeling and in the world at once, trying to look after both. Cancer is cardinal water, ruled by the Moon, and you build yourself around the people you care for and the home you make for them. Sagittarius, the card's sign, is five signs away, a quincunx, and it's fire. Fire and water are opposed elements. Put them in one pot and you get steam, or one of them puts the other out.

That friction is the honest centre of this pairing. Sagittarius wants out, the long trip, the big idea, the move interstate. Cancer wants in. You may feel both pulls in the same week, sometimes the same hour, an itch to go somewhere and a fierce wish to stay home and keep everyone close, and the quincunx means they never quite settle. You just keep adjusting by small degrees, which is tiring in a way that's hard to explain to anyone. The Chariot is Cancer's own Major, a driver in armour heading out. Temperance is gentler about it, and suggests you can go somewhere and still be the one who holds the family together.

At home it's the pull between minding your people and answering something bigger outside the family, a course, a job that means travel. With a parent it can be the conversation about whether you can go and still be there for them. Say yes to one thing further from home than you'd usually go, and plan how you'll check in while you're away.
sun.reversed:
Temperance reversed can make a Cancer Sun pull the shell in tight. The world outside starts to look like too much, so invitations get turned down, the trip gets cancelled, and looking after the family becomes the reason you never go anywhere. Fire and water don't mix well, and with the card upside down the Sagittarian push to go further tends to send you further back in.

Or you throw yourself at some big outside project and give it all the care you'd usually give your people, and home gets the tired leftovers. Either way it shows up at home first, in a family that's smothered or forgotten, and with a parent or a child who notices before you do. Ask someone at home what they'd like more of from you, and what they'd like less of, and take the answer seriously.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon is the Moon at home, feeling everything, remembering everything, needing somewhere safe to put it. You remember the song that was playing, what everyone wore, the exact thing your grandmother said when you left. Temperance is a healing card, and on the face of it that's good news for your tides. It's a Sagittarius card, though, and Sagittarius handles feeling almost the opposite way to you, lightly and with a lot of hope. It's also fire meeting your water.

What you'll recognise is a pull between feeling a thing all the way through and feeling better already. Part of you likes the lift in this card, the idea that things do mend. Part of you feels hurried by it, as though you're being told to cheer up about a sadness you haven't finished with. That's the fire and water in it. Too much warmth dries a feeling out before it's done, and too much water puts the hope out. Temperance at its best is the mix in between, a sadness allowed to be sad in the same evening as a bit of hope, with neither one winning.

It shows around the family home and the rituals that carry memory, a birthday, a recipe, a house being sold. Your appetite and your sleep will swing with it. Give yourself one evening that's allowed to be sad, with something good planned for the next morning, and keep both.
moon.reversed:
When Temperance turns over on a Cancer Moon, feelings can boil over in both directions. You're teary one minute and briskly fine the next, and you can't tell which feeling wants letting go and which you're scared to lose. The card's sign says move on. Your Moon says keep everything. Fire and water meeting like that doesn't make a pleasant, even warmth. It makes a lot of steam, and you end up frazzled.

It turns up in nights lost to nostalgia, scrolling old photos, and in holding onto people and places after they've changed. It turns up in the stomach, since a Cancer Moon's appetite rises and falls with its mood. Pick the one thing that's really ending and grieve that. Leave the older sorrows in their box for a while, and ring someone who'll just sit with you.

rising.upright:
Strangers often feel looked after by a Cancer rising before they've worked out why. You notice who hasn't got a drink, you remember the name of their dog, and you do all of it while quietly checking whether this person is safe to let in. The Moon rules your chart, so your face shows your mood more than you'd like. The card on your Ascendant is a Sagittarius card, and Sagittarius greets strangers like old friends, a big open hello and no checking at all. That's fire against your water, five signs apart, a quincunx, so the two ways of arriving don't really agree.

You may notice your guarded opening falling a bit short of what a situation wants. A new workplace, a friend's party, a first date, and you hang back reading for danger, and the moment where you could have joined in goes by. The card is fine with the care. It wants the warmth first and the checking afterwards. The Chariot is Cancer's Major, and its driver goes out into the world in armour, which makes sense for your sign. Temperance suggests taking the helmet off for the first five minutes. The adjustment is small and constant, and it won't feel natural for a while.

In a new job you might be seen as kind but hard to know. Meeting a partner's friends, your warmth can take an hour to show, and they've made up their minds in ten. Say hello first to one new person, before you've decided anything about them.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, Temperance can turn a Cancer Ascendant's caution into a wall with a kind face painted on it. You're polite, helpful even, and nobody gets any real access, because each new person is being assessed for how they might hurt you. The openness in the card can't get past that, and people sense they're being kept at the gate. Most of them stop trying.

The flip side is over-giving at the door, offering favours and food and help before anyone asks, so they'll like you. Your mood shows either way, since the Moon rules your chart. It turns up in a new job, in meeting neighbours, and with in-laws, where you've been lovely for years and they still don't really know you. Tell one person something small and true about yourself they didn't know, and leave it there.

sun.upright:
A Leo Sun is at its best with an audience. The launch, the first week in the new job, the party you're hosting, anything with a bit of occasion to it. The Sun rules Leo, fixed fire, and you're built to give off warmth and have it noticed, which is nothing to apologise for. Temperance comes from Sagittarius, four signs along and also fire. That's a trine, the easiest angle between two signs, and the card will feel like good company. Strength is Leo's own Major, and it has something in common with this one. In both cards someone is handling a lot of power gently, a lion in one and a stream of water in the other, and nobody's forcing anything.

The catch is that fire meeting fire turns the volume up, and what Temperance wants turned up is pacing. That's an odd request for a sign that likes to go big. You may be feeling it as a project you went all out on at the start, and now there's less in the tank for the long middle than you expected. You don't have to shine any less. The card wants it spread out so it lasts. Leo is fixed, so once you've settled on a way of doing things you tend to stick with it, and that's useful here, provided the way you settle on is one you can keep up.

In creative work it's the thing you poured yourself into early that now needs finishing without an audience. In love it's how you can fill a room so completely your partner has nowhere to stand. Choose one thing you're doing partly for applause and do it more quietly for a while.
sun.reversed:
Big openings and empty middles are the reversed Temperance in a Leo Sun. You go all in at the start, people clap, and the tank's dry for the unglamorous weeks where the real work happens. The trine with Sagittarius only feeds the flare, handing you a grander gesture whenever a steady one would have served you better.

Or it's a slump you cover with bravado. You're tired, you've given more than you had, and because you'd hate to be seen flagging you put on a bigger show. At work that looks like brilliant bursts and patchy follow-through. At home it's a partner who gets the performance and not much of you. Do one good piece of work that nobody will ever see or praise, and notice how it feels to know it's done.

moon.upright:
One short text can ruin a Leo Moon's evening, and one warm one can make its week. You need to feel loved out loud, warmth given back, a fuss made on your birthday, the sense you're someone's favourite. The Sun rules Leo, so this Moon runs warm, generous and a little dramatic, and it's lovely to be around when it's fed. The card's sign is Sagittarius, a fellow fire sign four signs along, and the trine means the card doesn't fight your feelings. It warms up alongside them. That's nice and slightly risky, because same-element pairings turn things up, and big is already your default.

What the card asks is that the highs and lows blend into something you can live in all week. A Leo Moon can go from delighted to crushed and back again before lunch. Temperance says the day doesn't have to swing that far. To you that can sound like being told to turn the music down, and something in you will resist, because the big version of a feeling seems more honest than the moderate one. It isn't, necessarily, and the people around you will find a steady warmth a lot easier to settle into.

With a partner it's how much of your mood depends on how they seem when they walk in the door. With friends it's how much you give, and the quiet tally you keep of what comes back. Next time you feel let down, wait an hour before you show it, and see whether it's still as big.
moon.reversed:
Every slight becomes a scene when this card is reversed for a Leo Moon. You feel overlooked, so you make sure everyone knows it, the sigh, the long silence, the exit with the door, and because Sagittarius is fire too it hands you the ultimatum when a quiet word would have done more. The feeling never gets to settle because it keeps being performed.

Sometimes the warmth dries up instead. You stop offering the generosity people count on and wait, a bit wounded, to see who notices. Both show up with a partner, and in friendships where you've started keeping score. People end up managing your moods and not meeting you in them, which is lonely for everyone. When the heat next rises, feel all of it privately first, and decide afterwards how much to show.

rising.upright:
Leo rising walks in and the room gets a bit warmer. You're noticed whether you want to be or not, and with the Sun as your chart ruler most people read you as confident, generous and a touch grand. Temperance on that doorway comes from Sagittarius, trine to Leo in the same element, so it settles onto your style without a fight. Both signs like an entrance. What the card adds is something Leo rising sometimes forgets, that the room doesn't have to be won in the first thirty seconds.

Same-element pairings amplify, so there's a risk of more wattage than a room can use. The useful side of this card is ease. When you slow the arrival by a beat, the warmth reads as real confidence and people trust it more, because it stops looking like it needs their applause to keep going. You may already have noticed that the quieter version of your first impression goes down better with certain people, often the ones you most wanted to impress.

With strangers it's the difference between dazzling someone and putting them at ease. In a new group it means holding some of your shine back so the others have room for theirs, and a new boss usually warms faster to that. At a wedding or a work do, go in without a story ready and let someone else tell the first one.
rising.reversed:
Each arrival turns into a small production when Temperance is reversed on a Leo Ascendant. You come in hot, and Sagittarius's love of a flourish keeps raising the stakes, so people feel performed at and never quite met. The warmth starts to read as need, which is the last thing you'd want.

Less obvious is the front that's gone dim. You've been knocked, maybe by a job or a break-up, and you're walking into rooms with the lights off, which people read as cold or proud when it's really tiredness. Look for it in first impressions that wear people out, or in the way one flat reaction from a stranger can sink your whole mood. Go to one thing without dressing up for it, say hello the way anyone would, and see who comes over.

sun.upright:
Virgo Suns like to get it right. You see the typo, the wobble in the shelf, the gap in the plan, and you fix it, often before anyone else knew there was a problem. Mercury rules Virgo, mutable earth, and your pride lives in the detail. Temperance comes from Sagittarius, three signs round from you. You're both mutable signs, and three signs apart in the same modality makes a square, the angle that creates friction and pushes you to act on it. On top of that the elements are neutral, fire and earth, so there's no easy warmth between the card and your Sun.

The pinch is between precision and trust. Sagittarius paints in broad strokes and assumes the details will sort themselves out. Temperance, Sagittarius's card, is a picture of someone adjusting a mix by feel, with no measuring jug and no checklist, and to a Virgo Sun that can look careless. The card's argument is that you've already got the blend about right, and it's the endless small corrections that keep throwing it off. The Hermit is Virgo's own Major, the card of looking closely, on your own, until you're sure. Temperance asks you to step back far enough to see the whole thing, and then leave it.

At work it's the report polished long past the point anyone would notice, when sending it would have been the better move. With your body it's a routine tuned so tightly it's become a stress of its own. Choose one thing to finish at good enough, send it, and don't open it again.
sun.reversed:
Nothing quite gets to done when Temperance is reversed for a Virgo Sun. There's always one more fix, one more read-through, and the square with Sagittarius means the pressure to act is there, it just goes into correcting and never into finishing. You stay busy, and things don't land.

Another version is harder on you than on anyone else. The critical eye turns inward and starts finding the flaw in you, your body, your work, the way you talk, until your confidence is worn thin. At work it's a project reworked so often it's lost its life. At home it's a list of self-improvements that only ever grows. Send one thing out with a rough edge still on it, then leave it alone and put up with the itch.

moon.upright:
The kitchen gets wiped down when a Virgo Moon is worried. A worry gets turned into a list, the small thing gets fixed so the bigger unease has somewhere to go, and most of the time it works. Mercury rules Virgo, and your feelings settle through sorting and being useful. Temperance reaches you from Sagittarius at a square, both of you mutable signs, and earth and fire have no particular pull toward each other, so the card doesn't soothe you. It prods.

What it's prodding at is the need to check. Temperance is a slow card, and a lot of what it describes happens where you can't see it, a body recovering, a friendship mending, a decision settling over a few weeks. You can't audit any of that, which makes a Virgo Moon twitchy, like leaving the house not quite sure the iron's off. The card is fairly clear that some things heal better when you stop touching them. That's a kind of care that looks a lot like doing nothing, and for you it takes nerve.

It shows around health worry, the symptom looked up at midnight, and around a relationship you keep trying to fix when what it mostly needs is time. Your stomach and your sleep will carry the tension before your head admits to it. Pick one worry and don't research it, raise it or fix it for three days, and see whether it's any worse at the end.
moon.reversed:
Care turns into fault-finding when this card is reversed in a Virgo Moon. You're looking for what's wrong, in yourself, in your health, in the people close to you, and the worry that's meant to keep everyone safe mostly keeps you braced. Sagittarius, the card's sign, would happily look at the bright, wide view. It can't get a word in.

It shows as a stomach in knots over a detail nobody else noticed, and in managing other people's routines so that nothing can slip, which they may or may not thank you for. It shows in sleep too, lying awake running through tomorrow's list. Mercury rules this Moon and likes to be useful. Choose one thing you'd normally correct in someone else and leave it as it is, and notice how long it takes to stop bothering you.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising meets people neatly. You come across as capable, observant and quietly useful, the one who's already spotted what needs doing, and Mercury as chart ruler gives you a quick, dry way of talking. Temperance on the Ascendant comes from Sagittarius at a square, and Sagittarius is as mutable as you are, so the two rub where they might have slid past each other. The elements don't help much either. Fire and earth neither clash nor click, so there's no automatic rapport.

The friction is in how you begin. Sagittarius opens the door wide and trusts things to work out, and Virgo checks the hinges first. You may notice your careful, helpful opening coming across as a bit cool, as if you're assessing people, which to be honest you usually are. The assessing is useful. It's also why some people keep a small distance at a first meeting. The card asks you to let some warmth out before you've finished vetting the situation, and the square keeps poking at that gap until you do something about it.

In a new job your competence gets noticed long before your kindness does. On first dates your quiet appraisal can read as unimpressed. With neighbours it might be the helpful note that comes across as a complaint. In your next first meeting, say one warm thing before you say anything useful.
rising.reversed:
A first meeting can start to feel like an inspection when Temperance is reversed on a Virgo Ascendant. You lead with what could be better, the correction, the slightly raised eyebrow, and the warmth the card could have brought stays behind your appraisal. People feel measured before they feel welcome, so they hold back too.

It can go the other way, where you're so anxious to be useful that nobody sees you at all, only the help. Both come from the same belief, that being useful is the safe way to be liked. At work you're respected and not always asked along. In dating, your standards arrive before your sense of humour does. Meet one new person without trying to help them with anything, and just enjoy their company.

sun.upright:
Libra's own Major is Justice, the figure with the scales. Temperance is the figure with the cups. Both are about balance, and a Libra Sun will feel at home with either, but they go about it differently, and that difference is what this draw is about. With scales you keep both sides separate and get them level. With cups you pour them together and end up with one thing.

Temperance comes from Sagittarius, two signs from Libra, a sextile, which is a friendly angle that opens a door and still needs you to walk through it. Fire and air get on, so the card's warmth and your cool sense of fairness move together easily. What you'll feel is a nudge past even-handedness. Ruled by Venus, cardinal air, you want everyone content and the split fair, and that can leave you forever adjusting the weights, a little to this side, a little to that. Sagittarius is a sign that picks a direction and says so. The card asks you to stop keeping score between two options and let them mix into something new, even if one flavour ends up leading.

In a partnership it's a scrupulously fair arrangement that's never become a shared plan. At work it's the decision you keep putting off because someone might mind. Take the two options you've been weighing, write down the best part of each, and build one plan out of those.
sun.reversed:
Pleasing everyone and choosing nothing is where a Libra Sun tends to land with this card reversed. You keep the peace by giving each side a little, so the mix never forms, and the life you're building ends up spread thinly across other people's preferences. Sagittarius is blunt and sure of itself, and upside down it just widens the gap between what you think and what you say.

Fairness can also go rigid. Everything has to be exactly even, the chores, the bill, whose turn it is to choose, and you're keeping a ledger nobody else knew existed. Look for it in a decision left open until it makes itself, and in a resentment you can't quite own because you agreed to everything. Choose the side you really lean toward in one small matter, and say so out loud.

moon.upright:
Tension in a room lands on a Libra Moon first. Someone's short with someone, the air goes tight, and you're already reaching for balance, smoothing, soothing, finding the thing both people can agree on. Venus rules Libra, and your comfort is bound up with harmony and with other people. Temperance comes from Sagittarius at a sextile, and since fire and air are friendly, the card's warmth blends readily with that need for calm. It's a kind pairing, with one catch you'll probably recognise.

Your version of peace can mean managing everyone else's feelings so well that you've lost track of your own. Temperance is about blending, and its point is that your own mood belongs in the mix, and you've been leaving it out. You tune yourself to what the room needs, and by the end of the day you couldn't say what you wanted for dinner, never mind anything bigger. Sagittarius has a name for saying what it thinks, and some of that comes with the card, a permission to feel something inconvenient and let it show. For a Libra Moon that's a real stretch, and it usually goes better than you fear.

With a partner it's swallowing a preference so there won't be a ripple. With friends it's being the peacemaker and going home drained. Next time someone asks what you'd like, answer before you've checked their face.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Libra Moon can dissolve into whoever it's with. You agree, you soothe, you mirror their mood back, and by evening your own feelings have gone somewhere you can't find them. The balance you've kept on the outside has cost you any on the inside. Sagittarius could steady you with a bit of plain truth, and your own diplomacy talks over it.

It shows as a mood that rises and falls with other people's, and in a slow resentment at always being the easy one. It can show in the body as tiredness after social things you told yourself you enjoyed. Venus rules this Moon, and Venus is also about what you value. Sit with one disagreement without smoothing it over, and notice where you actually stand once the discomfort passes.

rising.upright:
Libra rising is lovely to meet. You're pleasant, poised and easy to talk to, and people usually leave a first meeting with you feeling they came across well, which is a rare gift. Venus rules your chart. The card sitting on your Ascendant is Sagittarius's, two signs away at a sextile, and air and fire feed each other, so Temperance adds itself to your manner without any strain. What it brings is a steadier warmth underneath the polish.

A sextile offers an opening that still has to be taken. Your charm can be a smooth surface that keeps people comfortable and at a slight distance, and Sagittarius wants a bit of the unpolished you to come through the door as well. It's a sign that says what it thinks at a first meeting and gets away with it. When you let some of that in, the first impression moves from agreeable to trusted. It's a small shift, and people feel it quickly.

In interviews you might agree with everything and leave them unsure what you'd bring. In dating it's the difference between being liked and being known. In a new group it's letting one real opinion out early. At the next dinner with people you don't know well, cheerfully disagree with someone about something that doesn't matter much, and see what it does to the table.
rising.reversed:
Reversed on a Libra Ascendant, Temperance can turn the pleasant front into a surface nobody gets behind. You're agreeable with everyone and give nothing away, and the Sagittarian frankness that could make you real gets smoothed off before it reaches your face. People find you lovely and hard to know, and you can end up oddly alone in a room full of people who like you.

Or you become whatever each person seems to want, so different friends meet quite different people, until two of them end up at the same party. It's there in a first impression so accommodating it gives nobody anything to hold, and at work, where you're popular and passed over. Let one person meet the version of you that isn't managing their comfort, and trust them to cope.

sun.upright:
Moderation is close to a foreign language for a Scorpio Sun. You go all the way in or you don't go, you want the real thing under the surface, and you keep your power close. Scorpio is fixed water, ruled by Mars in the old scheme and Pluto in the modern one, and either way it's a sign that means it. Temperance, the card of the middle path, is about the least Scorpio card in the deck, and it's turned up for your light.

Sagittarius, the card's sign, sits right next to yours. Neighbouring signs have very little in common, and each has what the other lacks. What Sagittarius has is lightness, the belief that things will probably work out without being gripped, and what you have is depth. Fire and water are opposed elements as well, so where the card meets your Sun it gets heated. You may catch yourself distrusting the middle, sure that anything done at half strength is shallow or fake. Death is Scorpio's own Major, and Temperance is the card that follows it, fourteen after thirteen. In the order of the deck it's what comes after an ending, the slow business of putting things back together, and Scorpio Suns are often better at that part than they give themselves credit for.

With money and shared resources it's the all-or-nothing bet where a measured stake would have done. In intimacy it's the intensity you ask of people, which can scald. Take one thing you'd normally throw yourself into and do it at half strength for a while, and watch what happens to it.
sun.reversed:
All or nothing is the reversed Temperance in a Scorpio Sun, and it's usually all. Half measures feel like lying to you, so you go to the extreme, and the card's lighter side reads as not taking things seriously. You double down. The intensity that's your real strength starts burning the things it was meant to protect.

Sometimes it's nothing, a total withdrawal, where you cut something off completely because you couldn't have it the way you wanted. You'll see it in a grudge held long past its use, and in shared money handled like a test of loyalty. You'll see it in a closeness so intense there's no air in it. Loosen your grip on one thing you've been holding hard, even slightly, and see that it doesn't disappear when you stop squeezing.

moon.upright:
Scorpio Moons feel everything at full depth and show very little of it. You're loyal to the bone, slow to trust, and once someone's hurt you it takes a long time to forget, if you ever do. Temperance comes from the sign next door, Sagittarius, which handles feeling almost the opposite way, openly and quickly, with a lot of faith that it'll pass. Neighbours like these don't share much. Fire meets your water, and the two elements are opposed, so there's real friction in how each of you does emotion.

The card wants a feeling to move through at a moderate heat and then be let go. The letting go is where you'll struggle. Your instinct is to keep, the hurt and the love alike, and to keep them at full strength, as if feeling something less fiercely would mean it mattered less. Temperance offers a lower setting, and part of you will distrust it. There's healing on offer here, the slow kind, and that's about the only kind a Scorpio Moon has ever let anyone near.

It shows around trust, where you test people long after they've proven themselves, and in a hurt you nurse in private and haven't mentioned to anyone. Your body holds it as tension that doesn't quite let go, usually in the jaw or the shoulders. Is there an old grievance you could tell someone you trust, calmly, in a few sentences, and hear said at a normal volume?
moon.reversed:
Temperance upside down in a Scorpio Moon sends feeling underground. You won't show the hurt, so it turns into suspicion, a grudge, a quiet test the people around you keep failing without knowing they're sitting it. Sagittarius's easy warmth could let some light in, and to you it looks naive, so the lid stays on and the pressure goes up.

This can come out as jealousy you'd never admit to, or a loyalty so fierce it tips into keeping tabs on people. At its worst it's cutting someone off completely sooner than risk being hurt by them. It's in intimacy, and in family relationships that have been cool for years for reasons nobody says aloud. Tell one person something you feel while it's still small, before it has time to become a case against them.

rising.upright:
Very little gets given away in a first meeting with Scorpio rising, and people find that magnetic, or unnerving, or both. Mars rules your chart in the traditional system, and there's a watchfulness to how you come into a room, a sense you've clocked everyone before you've said a word. Temperance on your Ascendant is a Sagittarius card, and Sagittarius arrives open and unguarded, pleased to meet everybody. It's the sign next door to yours and nearly the reverse of your instinct. Fire against your water, too, so the two ways of arriving throw off some heat where they meet.

What the card offers is an easier door. It asks you to trust a stranger a fraction sooner than feels sensible, and to let people meet you without first having to earn their way past the guard, which most of them give up on before they get there. Sagittarius has the frankness you keep in reserve, the easy question, the unguarded laugh. Borrowing a bit of it costs you very little, and people who'd have drifted off after ten minutes might stay for an hour.

New colleagues may read your reserve as judgement. In dating the mystery draws people in and the guard sends a fair few of them away again, and in-laws can take years to feel they know you. In the next first meeting, answer one personal question fully, without deflecting, and notice who leans in.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising with this card reversed can turn the guard into a locked door. You reveal nothing, watch everything, and read each new face for the threat in it, and Sagittarius's warmth gets treated as a risk you can't afford. People feel scanned and shut out, and they stop trying.

There's an overcorrection too, where you've decided to be more open and it comes out as too much too soon, a big personal story in the first ten minutes, and then you regret it and close up harder. You'll see it in a manner that impresses from a distance and isolates up close, and in a suspicion that treats everyone new as guilty until cleared. Let one new person past the first checkpoint without making them prove anything, and see what they do with it.

sun.upright:
This is your card. Temperance is the Major of Sagittarius, so a Sagittarius Sun drawing it for their light is looking at their own sign's portrait, which doesn't happen often and is worth stopping for. Mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, you're the one aiming past the near thing at the big meaningful one, wanting room, saying what you think a little before you've finished thinking it. Card and Sun are the same element, so everything in this pairing runs large and bright.

The joke's on you a little, and I think you'll enjoy it. The card of your sign is the card of moderation. Jupiter thinks in more, further, bigger, and on your own sign's card an angel is pouring water from one cup to another so carefully that not a drop reaches the ground. It's the one lesson your temperament likes to dodge, handed to you as your own. Sagittarians I've read for usually laugh at this, and then go quiet, because they know which part of their life has been running on more when enough would have done.

With a big plan it's the promise made larger than you can deliver, and the fix is trimming it to a size you'll finish. In the body it's a restlessness that won't let you rest until something gives, often your sleep. Choose one horizon, one course or trip or project, and let the others wait until that one's done.
sun.reversed:
Saying yes to everything is how a Sagittarius Sun tends to wear this card reversed. The big trip, the new course, the side business, the friend's project, and Jupiter's appetite for more leaves you spread across three lives and properly present in none of them. Your own card wanted a steady pour into one cup. You're topping up every cup on the table at once.

It shows as a trail of enthusiasms started and dropped, and promises made in good faith that you can't keep, which people forgive the first few times. It shows in money too, spent on the next thing before the last one has paid off. Under it there's often a fear that picking one road means losing all the others. Pick one aim, give the rest up on purpose, and tell someone which you chose.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room. An open window, a plan for the weekend, the sense that you could go somewhere if you wanted to. When something hurts you look up and out, toward something bigger and brighter, and that's often how you get through. Temperance is your sign's own card, so drawing it for your tides is your inner weather looking at itself in the mirror. Same element, fire on fire, so the whole picture runs warm and wide.

What the card asks is the thing a Sagittarius Moon finds hardest, to stay put with a mood and let it settle where you are. Your instinct when something aches is to book a trip, find the silver lining, get moving. Temperance says let the extremes level out here, at home, in an ordinary week. The optimism is really yours, and it's a lovely thing. It can also be a way of never landing, and some part of you probably knows which feelings you've been outrunning. In my experience a feeling you sit with passes quicker than one you run from, which is annoying to hear and usually true.

At home it's the urge to escape whenever things get heavy or dull. In love it's needing an exit even when nothing's wrong, the half-packed bag you'd never admit to. Spend one evening inside a feeling without planning, booking or improving anything, and go to bed without having fixed it.
moon.reversed:
When your own card turns over, a Sagittarius Moon can treat every uncomfortable feeling as a reason to leave. You go, literally or in your head, toward the next plan, the next city, the next big idea, and Jupiter keeps handing you exits. The feeling you didn't sit with comes along in the luggage.

It shows as fresh starts that never deepen, and relationships you love right up until they ask you to stay. It can look like forced cheerfulness, too, the bright side found so fast that nobody gets to be sad around you, including you. Being pinned down feels worse to this Moon than almost anything, and that's the fear doing the driving. Cancel one escape you'd planned, a trip or a night out, and let yourself be bored at home.

rising.upright:
The loud laugh from the doorway is often Sagittarius rising. You come in open and enthusiastic, honest to a fault, already halfway to the next thing when you say hello, and with Jupiter as your chart ruler people usually meet someone generous and funny, with big gestures and bigger opinions. Temperance is your rising sign's own Major, which makes the card on your mask a close match for the face you already wear. Fire on fire, so the effect is large, warm and hard to miss.

The useful ask here is pacing. Your natural opening is generous and a lot, the strong view, the story, the plan floated before anyone's ready for it, and the card suggests letting yourself out a bit slower so people can keep up. Your frankness is a real gift, and it can land as too much too soon. Easing the entrance lets the warmth reach people without flattening them, and a big presence is easier to trust when it isn't trying to fill the whole room from the door.

With new colleagues the honesty that charms most people startles a few, and it's usually the few you'll need later. In a group of strangers the enthusiasm can crowd quieter people out. On a first date it's the travel stories. Go to your next new thing planning to ask three questions for every story you tell, and keep count.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising with this card reversed tends to overwhelm people before they've had a chance to settle. You arrive loud and certain, with the big claim, the blunt remark, the plan nobody asked for, and Jupiter keeps inflating the entrance past what a room can take. People step back. You read the gap as a need for more of you, so you give it.

First impressions dazzle and then tire people, and the bluntness stops being charming once the novelty wears off. It can show as the opposite, too, a sudden flat quiet when you're low, which people who've only met the big version don't know how to read. Walk into one room and say very little for the first half hour, and see who comes to find you.

sun.upright:
When Temperance turns up for a Capricorn Sun, the obvious reading, be patient, isn't news. You climb, you plan, you take the long view and trust effort over luck, and Saturn, which rules Capricorn, rewards exactly that. The more useful reading is that there are two kinds of patience and you mostly have one of them.

Yours is the patience of grind, of holding everything up and keeping your hand on the wheel. The card's sign, Sagittarius, sits right next to yours, and neighbouring signs have little in common, each carrying what the other goes without. What Sagittarius has is the patience of trust, letting a thing ripen without checking on it every hour. Jupiter, its ruler, tends to believe things will turn out, and in a Capricorn life that can feel almost reckless. Fire and earth are neutral elements, so there's no clash, just two strangers who need introducing. The Devil is Capricorn's own Major, a card about being chained to things. This card offers a looser hold, one that lets you keep what matters without gripping it.

At work it's the goal you've driven so hard you can't enjoy getting there. In the body it's running yourself like a machine and calling it discipline, and your back probably knows about it. Take one project that's going fine and stop checking on it for a fortnight.
sun.reversed:
Temperance reversed can turn a Capricorn Sun's patience into pure grind. You push through, you control the timeline, you carry the whole thing alone, and the idea that some things ripen on their own sounds to you like an excuse. So you tighten the screws, and the effort that built everything starts to cost more than it brings in.

A quieter form of it is aiming at nothing, because nothing felt worth the climb, and just maintaining. You'll find both at work, as overwork worn like a badge or ambition gone flat. You'll find them at home too, where the people you're providing for see less of you than they'd like. Leave one task unfinished on purpose one evening, and see that the structure holds without you.

moon.upright:
Asking for help is about the last thing a Capricorn Moon wants to do. Competence is comforting, a plan is comforting, and needing nobody is very comforting indeed. Saturn rules Capricorn, and emotionally that tends to mean feelings get handled like tasks, looked at, dealt with, filed. The card arrives from Sagittarius, the sign beside yours, whose way with feelings is almost foreign to you, warm and trusting and a bit careless. Neighbours share little, and your earth doesn't take to the card's fire by itself, so its ease won't get in unless you let it.

What Temperance wants is a feeling tended slowly and left out for a while, so it can soften. It's a healing card, and the healing it describes doesn't keep a schedule. For a Capricorn Moon that's exposing, the emotional version of being caught with your guard down at work. You'd sooner get it sorted. The card suggests some things can't be sorted, only lived with until they change, and that this is allowed.

You'll notice it in a self-reliance that keeps everyone at arm's length without you really meaning it to. Your shoulders hold what you won't feel. It can show with a parent, too, especially if the rule in your family was to cope quietly. Let someone carry something small for you, a lift, a meal, a job, and don't pay them back straight away.
moon.reversed:
Locked down is the word for a Capricorn Moon with Temperance reversed. Self-sufficiency becomes a fortress nobody's allowed into, including the parts of you that need something. You handle it, whatever it is, and any comfort on offer gets filed under indulgence. The feeling doesn't go anywhere. It goes cold and heavy and sits in the body.

It shows as carrying everyone and letting nobody carry you, and as a competence so complete that people stop offering. It shows in sleep, too, the kind that doesn't rest you because part of you is still on duty. Saturn rules this Moon and sets hard rules, and one of yours is probably that needing things gets you let down. Say one need out loud to someone safe, plainly, without apologising for it.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising meets people seriously. You come across as competent, self-possessed and a bit formal, someone you'd trust with something important, and Saturn as your chart ruler often gives you a reserve that strangers take a while to get past. Temperance on your Ascendant is a Sagittarius card, from the sign next door, and it arrives in a completely different way, warm and open and happy to be there. Neighbours have little in common, and fire on earth gives no natural spark, so the fit is an odd one.

What it offers is some lightness at the door, the sense that you don't have to prove yourself before you've taken your coat off. People already trust your seriousness. The warmth is what lets them like you, and I've seen Capricorn risings genuinely surprised by how much more comes their way once they're liked as well as respected. The card is asking you to take on a bit of that ease deliberately, since it won't arrive by itself.

At work your gravity impresses and can keep people a step away. In a new team, a joke from you early on would do more than another good idea. In dating it's the formality that reads as coolness. In the next first meeting, let yourself laugh at something before you've decided whether it's appropriate.
rising.reversed:
Reversed on a Capricorn Ascendant, the card can close your reserve into a door that reads as cold. You give nothing away, keep it professional, hold the distance, and any warmth on offer gets judged unserious. People respect you and don't come near, which suits the guard and starves the rest of you.

The subtler version is trying too hard to look relaxed, the forced joke, the casual clothes that look like a uniform, and people can tell. It's there in a manner so controlled you seem unreachable, and in an authority that keeps even friends a little formal. At family gatherings you've become the sensible one and nobody asks how you are. Let one person see you off duty, untidy and unsure about something, and see what happens to their respect.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns stand a little apart by choice. You think in systems and principles, you'd rather be true to an idea than fit in, and people often find you easier to admire than to get close to. Aquarius is fixed air, ruled by Saturn in the old scheme and Uranus in the modern one. Temperance belongs to Sagittarius, two signs away, a sextile. That's a friendly angle, an opening that's there if you take it, and since fire and air feed each other, the card's warmth and your cool ideas get on without much effort.

What the card brings to your detachment is heat. A mixture needs feeling in it as well as a good design, and Temperance is a card about getting your hands wet. You hold things at arm's length so you can see them clearly, and it works, it's why your judgement is good. Sagittarius nudges you to step in and mix with what you've been observing, the people as well as the problem. The Star is Aquarius's own Major, and there's a family likeness, since both cards show someone pouring water. In Temperance the water stays between two cups, close and careful, and that's the kind of closeness this card asks of you.

With a cause it's a principle defended so coolly that the people affected by it feel like data. With friends it's warmth you feel and keep behind glass. Pick one friend you've been meaning to see and see them in person, with no agenda.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with Temperance reversed can retreat so far into the idea that the people in it stop feeling real. You win the argument on principle, keep feelings at a clean distance, and any warmth on offer gets dismissed as sentiment. The mix never happens. You're right, and alone with it.

Or it swings the other way, into throwing yourself at a group or a cause so completely that you lose the independence you usually guard, and then pulling out abruptly when it gets too close. Look for it in caring about humanity in general while dodging the person in front of you, and in a coolness friends read as superiority. Ring one person you've been meaning to call, ask how they are, and keep the conversation on them.

moon.upright:
Temperance is a card about mixing things in, and an Aquarius Moon's first move with a feeling is to step back from it. You name it, explain it, maybe find it quite interesting, and keep a cool head where other people get swept away. That's a real strength in a crisis. The card comes from Sagittarius at a sextile, two signs away, and fire and air are friendly, so its warmth blends easily with your need for a bit of distance. The pairing works with you, and it offers a gentle way to let some heat back into feelings you've been keeping at a manageable temperature.

Your sense of safety comes from not being overwhelmed, and Temperance's point is that a moderate amount of real feeling won't overwhelm you. You can feel something properly and still be yourself afterwards. For an Aquarius Moon that middle ground, felt without being flooded, can be new, and uncomfortable the first few times. Saturn, the traditional ruler of Aquarius, likes feelings kept under control. Uranus, the modern one, likes to be free of them. Neither is much help when you're simply sad.

It shows around closeness, where you go cerebral the moment things get intimate, and in a loneliness you explain as preferring your own company. When feeling backs up, your body goes wired and restless. Next time something moves you, tell the person involved how you feel in one sentence, and don't add an explanation.
moon.reversed:
Every feeling gets filed under analysis when this card is reversed in an Aquarius Moon. You can explain your own heart like a case study, and warmth that might have got in is treated as a bit beneath you. The emotion doesn't vanish. It backs up behind the calm front and comes out as a wired, restless detachment, or a sudden cold withdrawal that surprises the people close to you.

It shows as grief thought about so thoroughly there seems nothing left to grieve, and as a self-sufficiency that has quietly become isolation. It shows with a partner who says they can't reach you. Let one feeling be messy and unexplained for an evening, and don't write about it or talk it through until the next day.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising meets people with a friendly sort of distance. You're interesting, original, a little unusual in how you dress or talk, and often the one standing slightly outside the group, by choice. Saturn is your chart ruler in the old system and Uranus in the new, and either way strangers pick up on independence. Temperance at your Ascendant belongs to Sagittarius, at a sextile, and since fire and air like each other the card's warmth takes to your style without a struggle.

What it offers is an arrival that's warmer and more present, so your originality reads as inviting where it could read as aloof. A sextile opens the door and then waits for you to use it. Your instinct at a first meeting is to watch for a while, and Sagittarius suggests you let some open warmth show sooner, a real smile, a question about them, the enthusiasm you usually save for people you know. When you do, people feel welcomed by the interesting person, and stop feeling held at a polite remove.

At parties and networking things you're remembered and not always approached. In a new job the detachment reads as not needing anybody, which is rarely true. On dates it's the irony you use to stay safe. At the next gathering, tell one person you're glad to see them, and mean it.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising with Temperance reversed can turn detachment into a permanent remove. You keep things cool and a little ironic, observe more than you join, and the warmth that might draw people in stays out of reach. People find you interesting, assume you don't want them, and leave you to it.

Or it flips, and you over-perform your difference, the deliberately odd opinion, the look designed to set you apart, so strangers meet the act before they meet you. It's there in a manner that's friendly on top and closed underneath, and in how you'll criticise a group you'd quite like to belong to. Online it can look like commenting on everything and posting nothing of your own. Drop the irony for one evening and say plainly what you like about the people you're with.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns feel their way through life. You're porous and kind, happiest when edges blur and things run into one another, and you often know what someone's feeling before they do. Temperance is Sagittarius's card, three signs from you, and you're both mutable, so that's a square, an angle that won't let you drift and keeps pushing you to act. The card's fire against your water adds friction on top. There's a family likeness underneath, though. In traditional astrology Jupiter rules both Sagittarius and Pisces, so the two signs share a streak of faith and generosity even while they rub each other the wrong way.

What the card asks is for your flow to take on a shape and a direction. Look at the water in the picture. It's going somewhere, from one cup to the other, and none of it is spilling. Your gift is dissolving into things, the feeling, the music, the other person, and Temperance wants some of that poured into one channel that actually leads somewhere. The square makes it uncomfortable on purpose, pushing a sign that would happily float to point itself. The Moon is Pisces's own Major, a card of half-light and uncertain paths, and next to it Temperance is a steady card to have on your side.

In creative work it's the lovely thing never finished because finishing means choosing. With a partner it's merging until you can't find yourself. Give one drifting project a deadline, and tell someone what it is so you can't quietly let it go.
sun.reversed:
Temperance reversed lets a Pisces Sun lose its outline altogether. You merge into whatever's around you, dodge the edges of a decision, let the days blur into each other, and the Jupiter that Pisces shares with the card's sign only widens the fog. Without a channel the flow spreads and thins until nothing has much force.

It shows in gentle escapism, screens, daydreams, a drink or two more than you meant, anything that softens the edges. It shows in a sense of self so merged with other people's that you've gone missing from your own life. Under the drift there's often a fear that a firm shape would cost you the open feeling you love. Pick one thing to be definite about, a no, a date, a price, and hold to it for a week.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon takes in every feeling in the room, its own and everyone else's, and deals with the hard ones by drifting somewhere gentler, into music, sleep, a book, a daydream. Temperance reaches you from Sagittarius at a square, both of you mutable, so the card prods where a friendlier angle would soothe. Fire meeting your water adds friction. Still, they're not strangers. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and holds the older claim on Pisces as well, so there's some warmth under the rub.

The card is asking for some shape around what you feel. Your feelings don't have many edges, and Temperance wants them measured enough that they don't swamp you or spill onto everyone nearby. A Pisces Moon can hear that as being told to feel less. It's closer to being handed a cup to hold the feeling in, so you can see how much of it there is and whose it is.

It shows around soaking up other people's moods until you can't find your own, and around escaping into sleep or screens when it gets to be too much. Your energy tracks the emotional weather closely, and a hard day at work can take two days to wear off. Before bed, go through the day's feelings and work out which were actually yours, and let the borrowed ones go.
moon.reversed:
Flooded is a fair word for a Pisces Moon with Temperance reversed. The line between your feelings and everyone else's goes, and you go under in the mix. You carry griefs that aren't yours and slip off into fantasy when things get heavy, and the card's urge toward somewhere brighter only helps you leave.

You'll see it as exhaustion after time with upset people, even when all you did was listen. You'll see it as a retreat into sleep, daydreams or something numbing when life presses in, and in a softness that makes it hard to say no to anyone. Tenderness is what this Moon lives for, and firm edges can feel like they'd cut you off from it. Say one real no to someone, kindly, and notice how much steadier you feel afterwards.

rising.upright:
People tell Pisces rising things within ten minutes of meeting them that they wouldn't tell anyone else. You meet the world softly, gentle, receptive and a bit hard to pin to one shape, and with Jupiter as your traditional chart ruler and Neptune as the modern one, strangers often come away with quite different impressions of you. Temperance on the Ascendant comes from Sagittarius at a square, both mutable signs, so it nudges where it might have eased. The card's fire against your water adds some friction, though Jupiter has a hand in both signs, which gives the pairing more warmth underneath than you'd expect.

What the card asks is a clearer way in, an entrance that actually arrives. Your instinct is to take on the mood of the room and let people see what they want in you, and it makes you very easy to be around. Sagittarius walks in and says something definite. The square makes that pull hard to ignore. People are trying to work out who you are, and giving them one clear thing to hold onto, an opinion, a preference, a plan, helps them find you.

At work you might be liked by everyone and remembered by nobody in particular. In a new friendship group you can blend in so well you disappear. On dates it's letting the other person decide everything. Go into the next meeting with one clear thing you want from it, and say it in the first ten minutes.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, Pisces rising can become so soft it barely registers. You blend into whatever's wanted, mirror the room, let your edges go, and people sense someone kind without being able to say who. So they fill in the blank themselves, and not always the way you'd want.

There's also a vagueness you put up on purpose, being elusive because being definite feels risky. It's in first impressions that are all atmosphere and no outline, and in a habit of becoming whatever each person needs until there's not much of you left over. Listen for how often you say 'I don't mind'. Show one clear edge in your next conversation, a real preference, and let someone meet the shape of you.

1.upright:
Your body, your bearing and how you begin things all belong to the first house, and Temperance drawn here is about pace. How fast you walk into a room, how quickly you commit, how much energy you spend in the first ten minutes of anything. It's an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, so whatever's going on here tends to be visible to other people before it's obvious to you.

Aries is the first house's natural sign and Mars its natural ruler, which makes this corner impatient by nature, all first moves. Temperance's sign, Sagittarius, is trine to Aries and made of the same fire, so the card and the house get on easily, and the pairing turns up the volume on whatever you're already putting out. That can be lovely. You may come across as warm, capable and in no hurry, someone who acts without flailing. It can also mean a lot of beginnings and not much staying power, because fire on fire likes starting things. Mercury has its joy in this house, which adds a quick tongue to the mix, and with Temperance here you may find yourself thinking before you speak a bit more often than usual.

In the body it favours energy that lasts, meals at regular times, exercise you can keep up, sleep that isn't borrowed against. In how you present, people may start treating you as the steady one in the group. If you're starting something new, a job, a routine, a relationship, start it at a pace you could keep for a year.
1.reversed:
The reversed card in the first house is usually all start and no follow-through. The fire in how you present runs too hot, so you throw yourself at people and projects with a big opening and not much left for the second week. Since the card and the house share an element, the excess feeds itself. People meet a lot of energy and can't always keep up.

It shows in a body run ragged by too many starts and not enough rest, and in first impressions that promise more than they settle into. Sometimes it's the other extreme, a flatness after you've burnt through so much that getting going on anything feels hard. Mars rules this house naturally and likes to push through. Slow down the way you begin things, and let one new habit prove itself before you add a second.

2.upright:
The second house is the pay that comes in, the savings that do or don't build up, and the quieter sense of what you're worth. It's succedent, one of the houses that builds up and holds on, and its natural sign is Taurus, ruled by Venus, which likes security and nice things in about equal measure. Temperance brings a moderate, even hand to all of it, neither hoarding nor splashing out.

The fit isn't smooth, though. Sagittarius, the card's sign, is five signs from Taurus, a quincunx, and the two share almost nothing. Fire and earth are neutral elements as well, so the card's expansiveness and the house's wish to hold on have to be introduced and talked into cooperating. What you'll probably feel is a pull between spending on experience, the trip, the course, the thing that makes life bigger, and keeping something solid underneath you.
