Jupiter, Sagittarius's ruler, is generous and optimistic about money. Taurus wants to see it in the bank. Temperance sits between them, and on a good day that means money coming in and going out in a way that actually balances.

With your finances it favours a steady budget over a big bet or a sudden cutback, with a set amount for the life-widening things and a set amount that never gets touched. With your sense of worth it's noticing that what you're worth doesn't go up and down with the balance. Set up an automatic transfer, however small, into an account you don't look at, and a second one for the thing you've been wanting to do.
2.reversed:
Feast then famine is the usual shape of this card reversed in the second house. There's a run of spending on the next big experience, then the earthy side of the house panics and clamps down, and you swing between plenty and scarcity with nothing steady in between. The quincunx between Sagittarius and Taurus means this placement never finds a rhythm easily.

You'll know it by the way you check the balance, often or never, and the mood that follows. It's there in a sense of worth that rises and falls with what you've got, generous and confident on payday and small by the end of the fortnight. Venus rules this house and likes to be comfortable. Write down one plain, boring rule for your money, how much goes where each pay, and follow it for three pay cycles before you change anything.

3.upright:
Everyday talk lives in the third house. Messages, errands, the drive to the shops, siblings, neighbours, the course you're doing at night, all the small back-and-forth of a week. It's cadent, a house of learning and adjusting, and Temperance suits that. The card's sign, Sagittarius, is directly opposite Gemini, the third house's natural sign, so the two ends of one axis meet here, the near, detailed mind and the far, big-picture one.

Air and fire are friendly, so the meeting is lively and doesn't turn into a fight. What you'll notice is the tug between the fact in front of you and what it all adds up to. Mercury rules the third, and Mercury likes information. Jupiter, Sagittarius's ruler, likes meaning. With Temperance here you can become the person who holds several views at once and pours them into one balanced take, which comes in handy in any family argument. The Moon has its joy in this house too, so a lot of this happens through feeling, the tone of a voice note, the text you reread three times.

With a brother or sister it could be the conversation where you finally find the middle between two old positions. In learning it's pacing yourself through something long, a language or a qualification, without cramming. Around the neighbourhood it's the regular chat with someone you'd only ever nodded to. Before you send the next message that matters, read it through once just for tone.
3.reversed:
The third house with Temperance reversed talks in every direction and lands nowhere. The pull toward the big statement runs past the details, so you argue the grand point and miss what the other person said, or start six books and finish none. Opposite Gemini, the house's own sign, the placement tips into all breadth and no grip.

It can go the other way, where you've gone quiet, stopped replying, let the small contacts lapse because they felt pointless next to the bigger things. With siblings old arguments restart word for word. The mind skims and doesn't take much in. Pick one thread you've been neglecting, a message, a call, a half-finished course, and see it through to a proper end.

4.upright:
Home is the fourth house. The actual place you live, the family you came from, and the private ground you stand on when nobody's watching. It's angular, a corner of the chart, so what goes on at home tends to set the tone for everything else. Temperance here is working to keep the household balanced, with different people's rhythms and needs blended into something everyone can live with.

It's not a natural fit. Cancer is the fourth's natural sign, ruled by the Moon, and it's water. Sagittarius is fire, and the two are five signs apart, a quincunx. Fire and water are opposed elements, so there's friction, a restless, outward energy in the one part of the chart that wants to feel settled and safe. You may feel it as a pull between putting down roots and keeping the door open, a bag half packed, a move you keep talking about, a family you love and need a break from. The Moon rules this house and likes things to stay as they are. Sagittarius gets restless when they do. The card's work is to find a version of home with room for both.

With family it can look like the job of blending very different needs around one table, a partner's family and your own, a teenager and a grandparent. In the house itself it might be changing a room so it stops feeling stuck. If you're caring for a parent, it's pacing that care so you don't burn out. Have people over, and cook something that brings two sides of the family together.
4.reversed:
A home that won't hold still is the usual sign of Temperance reversed in the fourth house. The itch for somewhere else runs hot against family life, and fire meeting the house's water makes it hard for anyone to settle. You might be always coming and going, or always planning to leave, or keeping family at a warm distance so nobody can pin you down.

Sometimes it turns inward, and home becomes somewhere you hide from the rest of your life, door shut, phone off, the family carrying on around you. You'll hear it in arguments about who does what, and feel it in a house that's become a stopover. With parents, old patterns can replay at every visit. Stay put long enough for one room to feel properly yours, and spend real time in it with the people you live with.

5.upright:
Delight is the fifth house's territory. Flirting, making things, kids, a game of cricket in the park, a free afternoon with nothing booked. It's succedent, a house that builds up what it holds, and its natural sign is Leo, ruled by the Sun. Venus has her joy here. Temperance's sign, Sagittarius, is trine to Leo, both fire, so the card lands easily and tends to turn the pleasure up.

That's mostly good. There's a lot of warmth in this placement, a readiness for fun and a generous streak. The card's particular contribution is pace, enjoying things at a rate you can keep up. Fire on fire likes the next thrill and the bigger adventure, and without some temperance it'll burn through every pleasure at speed and wonder why none of them lasted. With it, a creative project or a new romance gets to unfold at its own rhythm, and you get to be present for the thing you're in. Sagittarius is the sign of the long trip, and its idea of fun is often bigger than the budget, which the fifth house doesn't always notice.

In a creative project it favours steady making, a bit most days, over one wild weekend. In romance it's letting attraction build at its own warm pace. With children, yours or anyone's, it's patient play, the game that goes on for an hour because nobody's rushing. Take one hobby you've dropped and give it a regular slot in the week.
5.reversed:
Chasing pleasure until it stops being pleasant is the fifth house with Temperance reversed. The fire here, doubled by the trine with Leo, goes from thrill to thrill, the next romance, the next creative high, the next big night, and never stays long enough to enjoy any of them. Venus has her joy in this house, and she can't find much to enjoy in a rush.

The opposite happens too. Fun gets rationed so strictly, all diets and budgets and early nights, that there's no play left at all. Creative projects fizzle after the first burst, and romance holds your interest only until it's certain. With children it can show as impatience with slow games. Choose one pleasure and have it properly, all the way through, before you look for the next.

6.upright:
Upkeep is the sixth house's business. The work as it really goes on a Tuesday afternoon, what's in the fridge, whether you walked anywhere, the small maintenance a body needs to keep going. It's cadent, a house of adjusting and processing. On the face of it Temperance could hardly land anywhere better suited, since moderation and steady rhythm are the whole point of the card, and here they meet the house that looks after the day to day.

The astrology complicates it a little. Sagittarius, the card's sign, squares Virgo, the sixth house's natural sign, and both are mutable, so there's friction that pushes you to do something. Sagittarius does wellbeing in broad strokes, get outside, feel good, it'll be fine. Virgo, ruled by Mercury, wants the details, the step count and the food diary. Earth and fire sit neutrally with each other, so the big good intention and the fiddly daily discipline have to be married on purpose. Mars has its joy in the sixth, which gives the house an appetite for effort. With this card that effort does best going into something moderate you do every day, and worst when it lurches between a health kick and total neglect.

With the body it favours steady upkeep, a walk most days, regular meals, bed at roughly the same hour. At work it's a pace you can hold across the whole week without a collapse on Friday. If you look after someone else day to day, a child, a parent, a dog, it's making sure your own upkeep is on the list as well. Choose one small habit, give it a set time, and keep it going until you stop having to think about it.
6.reversed:
Daily upkeep swings between extremes when Temperance is reversed in the sixth house. You go all in on a regime, the early gym, the strict diet, the colour-coded planner, and then drop it completely, or you ignore the routine until something forces your hand. The square with Virgo, the house's own sign, fights the very detail that would keep you well.

At work the week swings between frantic and flat. In the body there's a tiredness that doesn't lift, or a niggle you keep ignoring. It can show as a routine that's become punishing, exercise done as penance. Mars has its joy here and likes effort, which isn't always the same thing as looking after yourself. Pick one moderate habit, the most boring one you can think of, and hold it steadily until it sticks.

7.upright:
Temperance drawn into the seventh house looks a lot like a description of a good partnership. Two different people, two rhythms, blended without either one disappearing. The seventh is the house of the person across from you, whether that's a partner, a co-founder, a landlord you've signed with, or someone you're openly at odds with, and it's angular, so these relationships sit right at the front of your life.

Libra is the seventh house's natural sign and Venus its ruler. Sagittarius is two signs from Libra, a sextile, and fire and air feed each other, so cooperation comes readily. A sextile is an opening you still have to walk through, though. What you'll notice is the business of mixing two lives into one workable whole, and all the small negotiations that takes. Sagittarius brings honesty and warmth to it, and a need for some freedom inside the relationship. Venus brings the wish to keep things fair and pleasant. Temperance adds the patience to find a mix where neither person is always the one giving way. One of you may be quick and the other slow, one a saver and one a spender, and the card is interested in how the two get poured together.

With a partner it's the daily work of two tempos finding one, the weekend plans, the money, whose family you see on the holidays. In business it's a deal reached by degrees, with some give on both sides. If you're single, it can be meeting someone whose life fits alongside yours without either of you shrinking. Sit down with the person opposite you and work out one thing you'd both like more of.
7.reversed:
Lopsided is the word for the seventh house with Temperance reversed. The balance between two people tips and stays tipped, one of you pouring and the other receiving, and whoever's pouring is getting tired of it. The Sagittarian streak here can go either way, overwhelming a partner with too much, or keeping one foot out the door so you never quite commit.

It shows in who pays, who plans, who apologises first, and in a pattern of needing an escape route even with someone good. In business it can be a contract signed too freely and regretted later. Venus rules this house naturally and wants things fair. Ask the person opposite what they'd change about how things are shared between you, and hear the whole answer before you reply.

8.upright:
Shared money and shared lives belong to the eighth house. The joint account, a loan you're paying off together, what a parent might leave you, sexual intimacy and the trust it needs. Endings belong here as well, and what they make of you. It's succedent, a house where things build up, for good or ill. Temperance is a card of moderation landing in territory that runs on intensity, so it has some work to do to belong here.

Scorpio is the house's natural sign, ruled by Mars in the old system and Pluto in the modern one. Temperance's sign, Sagittarius, is Scorpio's next-door neighbour, and neighbouring signs share very little. Fire meets the house's water too, and those are opposed elements, so expect some friction. What the card brings is an even temper where things usually go all the way down. Deep intimacy tends toward extremes, and Temperance asks for trust built by degrees. Shared money wants the same steady handling. There's a risk in it as well, since Sagittarius likes to keep things light and free, and the eighth house doesn't let anyone stay light for long.

With joint finances it favours a slow, honest evening-up of what each person brings and owes. In intimacy it's closeness that deepens at a pace both people trust. If something is ending, a relationship, a job, a whole chapter, the card suggests ending it gradually and cleanly, with the loose ends tied. If you share money with someone, agree on one amount each of you can spend without asking, and one kind of decision you'll always make together.
8.reversed:
The eighth house with Temperance reversed loses its footing in deep water. The wish to stay light rubs against everything this house asks, so you either dodge real closeness and shared commitment, or plunge in and then bolt when it gets heavy. Fire and water keep fighting here, and the shared ground doesn't settle.

It shows in joint money handled carelessly, or kept so separate that the partnership never really merges. It shows in a closeness you back away from just as it deepens, and in endings left messy because you'd sooner not look at them. An inheritance or a debt can bring it all out. Stay with one hard conversation about money or closeness past the point where you'd usually change the subject.

9.upright:
This is the house Temperance belongs to. Sagittarius, the card's sign, is the ninth house's natural sign, and Jupiter, which rules Sagittarius, is the house's natural ruler, so the card is standing on its own ground. The ninth is belief, higher study, long-distance travel, other cultures, the law, and the search for what it all adds up to. It's cadent, a house where understanding gets worked through, and the Sun has its joy here, which warms things further.

Home ground amplifies everything. You may feel a strong pull toward something larger, a qualification, a trip that's more than a holiday, a set of ideas you want to understand properly. The card is about pursuing it at a pace that actually gets you there. The danger with a placement this comfortable is overreach, so much faith and appetite for the far horizon that you skip the steady steps in between. Look at the path in the picture, winding away from the pool toward a light in the distance. It's a long way, and the angel isn't running. Study done slowly tends to change how you think, and belief that's been tested against ordinary life tends to hold.

In learning it's the long course over the quick certificate. With travel it's the trip where you stay in one place long enough to understand it. With faith or philosophy it's letting an idea ripen before you pick up the next one. Choose one book, course or place that matters to you and stay with it until you've properly finished.
9.reversed:
On its own ground and upside down, Temperance in the ninth chases meaning so hard it never arrives anywhere. The fire runs unchecked, so you collect beliefs, plans and destinations and settle into none of them, always aimed at the next horizon. The steady steps that turn searching into understanding get skipped.

It can also be certainty gone too far, one belief held so hard that everyone who disagrees is simply wrong. Look for study started and dropped, a faith swapped every year or two, and a restlessness that mistakes moving for growing. With in-laws or people from other backgrounds it can come out as preaching. Stay with one path of learning or belief long enough to be changed by it before you look for another.

10.upright:
What you're known for, and what you're working toward in the world, is the tenth house's territory. The job title, the reputation, the name people put to you when you're not in the room. It's angular and sits at the top of the chart, so what happens here is visible and tends to be decisive. Temperance here builds a public life by measured, sustainable steps, the kind of steadiness that outlasts people who sprint.

Capricorn is the tenth's natural sign and Saturn its natural ruler, and Saturn likes hard work over a long time. Sagittarius comes just before Capricorn on the wheel, and neighbouring signs like these have little in common. Fire and earth don't pull together naturally, so Sagittarius's faith and reach and Capricorn's cool ambition have to be brought together deliberately. What you may feel is a tension between wanting your work to mean something big and wanting to climb steadily. Jupiter, Sagittarius's ruler, aims at meaning. Saturn aims at the top. Temperance keeps you from burning out on the climb, and from spreading yourself across too many goals at once.

In your job it favours steady progress across years, and mixing skills together, the technical and the human, the old job and the new interest. With a boss or a board it's being known for good judgement and following through. If you run your own thing, it's growing it at a pace that doesn't eat your weekends. Look at your working week and cut one thing that's only there to look busy.
10.reversed:
A career under Temperance reversed tends to go in several directions and build none of them. The reach overshoots, so you chase more ambitions at once than anyone could carry, or pour everything into the job until the rest of your life thins out. Next to Capricorn's patient climb, the placement is short on the steadiness that turns effort into a name.

It shows in a work history of big moves that never add up, and in a reputation for promise ahead of delivery. With a manager it might be a habit of overpromising. It can show as burnout dressed up as ambition, or the reverse, a public life you've quietly stopped caring about. Saturn rules this house and rewards patience. Pick the one goal at work that matters most and let the others wait their turn.

11.upright:
The eleventh house holds the people you choose and the future you're hoping for, your friends, the clubs and teams and online circles you belong to, the long-range wishes. It's succedent, building up what it holds, and it's one of the friendliest houses in the chart for this card. Jupiter, Sagittarius's ruler, has its traditional joy in the eleventh, so the card's own planet is especially happy here.

Aquarius is the house's natural sign, with Saturn as its traditional ruler and Uranus the modern one. Sagittarius makes a sextile to Aquarius, two signs apart, and air feeds fire, so the card and the house cooperate well. What the card brings is balance to the group and some measure to your hopes. There's generosity here, a warmth that pulls different people together and aims at a broad, hopeful future. At its best you're the one who can mix a group of quite different friends and keep a shared plan grounded enough to happen. The risk is giving too much to one part of your circle and not enough to another, or letting a hope swell until no number of steps would reach it.

With friends it's the even hand that keeps a group in balance, the one who makes sure the quiet person gets asked along. In a club, a team or a community project it's the patient organiser who gets things done by degrees. With your hopes for the future it's dreaming big and then breaking the dream into steps you can take. Introduce two friends from different parts of your life who you think would get on.
11.reversed:
Temperance reversed in the eleventh house usually means the balance in your circle has gone. You give a lot to one friend or one group and let the others drift, or your hopes for the future have swollen until they've lost touch with any real steps. Even with Jupiter in its joy here, the measure goes out of it.

It shows in friendships that run hot and then cold, in being either the centre of every plan or nowhere to be seen, and in grand plans that never get a foothold. It can show in money around friends, too, the dinners you always pay for. Saturn, the house's traditional ruler, likes things built properly. Get back in touch with a friend you've let slide, and cut one big hope down to a first step you can actually take.

12.upright:
What happens when nobody's watching, including you, is the twelfth house. Sleep, time alone, the retreat you take when the world gets loud, and the slow processing that goes on underneath all of it. It's cadent, a place where things get worked through and let go. Temperance here does its blending out of sight, a slow inner reconciling that carries on while you rest.

Pisces is the twelfth's natural sign, with Jupiter as its traditional ruler and Neptune its modern one. Sagittarius squares Pisces, both mutable, and it's fire against water, so there's friction, a sign that wants to be up and doing sitting in a house that asks you to stop. The two do share Jupiter, which gives the placement a thread of faith under the rub. Saturn, oddly, has its joy in this house, and that matters with this card, since a restless sign does better in the twelfth with some edges around the quiet, the same time for lights out, a morning that starts slowly on purpose. What the card describes is a healing you can't fully manage or watch, the sense of being put back together without supervising it. That's hard for the Sagittarian side of the card, which likes to see where it's going.

With sleep it favours real rest over constant motion, the phone out of the bedroom, the same wind-down each night. With the private side of life it's time alone that restores you, a walk with no destination, a long bath. If you're recovering from something, it's trusting that the mending is happening even when you can't feel it. Book a stretch of time with nothing in it and don't fill it.
12.reversed:
The twelfth house with Temperance reversed won't let the hidden work happen. The part of you that needs to move and aim fights the stillness this house requires, so you avoid being alone, fill every quiet moment with noise, and never let rest do its mending. Squared to Pisces, with fire meeting water, the inner ground stays churned up.

Sometimes it's the reverse, a retreat that's gone on too long, hiding from the world in sleep or screens or something numbing. It shows in not being able to sit alone with yourself, and in exhaustion you won't slow down long enough to feel. Dreams can be restless and crowded. People close to you may only see the busyness and not what it's covering. Allow one stretch of real stillness, uncomfortable as it is, and let something settle while you're not watching it.
